text:
maria: Heads up — perf regression observed on mistral-14b after the AWQ calibration landed this morning. p99 token time +35% on our synthetic chat workload. Repro steps attached below.

sam: Ouch. Any traces or profiler output?

maria: Pasting the lightweight trace snippet from the runtime profiler: 
```
[profile] model=mistral-14b seq=1024 batch=8
kernel_selector: chose awq_int8_conv (fast) for most ops
BUT: for attention @ layer 18-22 selector fell back to slow_matmul_fallback
reason=rope_scale_mismatch, kv_stride=64 -> split path
token_ms: p50=9ms p95=75ms p99=210ms (baseline pre-calib p99=155ms)
kv_cache_evictions: ~3% of requests triggered small warmups (extra memcpy)
```

jordan: That "rope_scale_check" is new; it validates RoPE frequency scaling for head dim mismatch after quantization. The check likely trips when scaled sin/cos precision drops below threshold for AWQ kernels. Might need to relax it or selectively run a higher-precision path only for RoPE-sensitive layers.

ryan: Quick numbers from local perf-run:
- baseline (gptq fp16-like): 460 tok/s, p99 150ms
- awq (post-calib): 430 tok/s, p99 205ms
- awq w/ selector-gate disabled: 445 tok/s, p99 170ms
accuracy deltas on our summary prompts: AWQ -0.8% vs GPTQ, FP8 -1.5% (but FP8 had better tok/s)

sam: Can you dump the kernel selection log for the problematic layers? e.g., which kernels were ranked and why fallback happened. Also want the batch size distribution — the scheduler might be micro-batching more now.

maria: Uploading kernel-log excerpt: 
```
layer 18: candidates=[awq_int8_conv, matmul_opt_v2, slow_matmul_fallback]
awq_int8_conv: score=0.82 pass=quantized_kvcheck fail=rope_scale_check
matmul_opt_v2: score=0.79 pass=rope_scale_check fail=tile_align
slow_matmul_fallback: score=0.65 pass=everything
=> selected slow_matmul_fallback
```

jordan: That "rope_scale_check" is new; it validates RoPE frequency scaling for head dim mismatch after quantization. The check likely trips when scaled sin/cos precision drops below threshold for AWQ kernels. Might need to relax it or selectively run a higher-precision path only for RoPE-sensitive layers.

ryan: Also noticed KV cache warmup spikes whenever a request is routed to a different device kernel (cache layout differs). For Mistral's big-head design, a head/kv stride mismatch can force a different layout and cause memcpy + recompute of cached keys. That's adding ~8-12ms in the hot path.

sam: Proposed quick mitigations: 
- runtime: tighten kernel-selector scoring to prefer awq_int8_conv when rank delta < 0.05 and seq<512
- scheduler: avoid splitting batches across kernel variants when possible (prefetch affinity)
- quant-team: rerun calibration with RoPE-specific prompts (short/long) and a few random long-context chats to capture sin/cos drift

maria: I've pushed a temporary gate that prevents rope_scale_check from forcing fallback for layers < 24 and seq <= 512. Rolling to canary now.

ci-bot: perf-run #789 finished: canary=2419801299
Summary: canary vs prod (mistral-14b, mix load): p99 down from 205ms -> 162ms, tok/s up 3.5%.

sam: Nice. Can we get accuracy numbers on the same canary? Want to ensure the gate doesn't regress AWQ quality.

ryan: Ran eval on calibration prompts:
- calib_short (5-20 tokens): AWQ pre-fix acc 92.4% -> post-fix 92.1% (delta -0.3)
- calib_long (512+ tokens): AWQ pre-fix 88.7% -> post-fix 88.6% (delta -0.1)
- edge_rope (frequent positional shifts): pre-fix 81.2% -> post-fix 80.9% (delta -0.3)
So small dips but within noise.

maria: Good. Action items:
1) sam: run GPTQ baseline + FP8 runs for the same canary config, capture kernels chosen (deadline EOD)
2) ryan: assemble a 200-prompt RoPE calibration set (short/med/long + adversarial shifts)
3) jordan: explore relaxing rope_scale_check or adding a quantized RoPE compensation kernel (preferably single-op shim)

jordan: Quick note — for mixtral/mistral differences, head dimension disparity requires that our kernel tiler support stride=32/64 variants. I'll prototype a tile_align patch that will let matmul_opt_v2 accept the layout without fallback.

maria: Thanks. If the patch looks risky, we'll keep the gate and plan a proper rollout with perf+quality gates.

sam: FYI I'll also test scheduler affinity changes to reduce micro-batch splitting — that alone historically shaved ~6-10% off p99.

maria: Thanks all. Will post results from the canary run and update the incident if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: incident-note: linked perf regression ticket #INFR-2311 updated by maria
